core_obligations: Construct the boundary maps δ_n : M_n → N_n = H^{p+1}(X, I^nF_{n+1}) from the short exact sequences 0 → I^nF_{n+1} → F_{n+1} → F_n → 0 and show ⊕Im(δ_n) is a graded submodule via the commutative diagram giving δ_{n+m}(fs) = fδ_n(s) (proof lines 8951-8973).

Finite generation: by ACC choose generators δ_{n_j}(s_j), set c = max(n_j); for n > c and s ∈ M_n write δ_n(s) = Σ f_j δ_{n_j}(s_j) with f_j ∈ I^{n-n_j} and lift s − Σ f_j s_j to an element of M_{n+1} (proof lines 8974-8982).
Conclude Im(M_{n+1} → M_{n-c}) = Im(M_n → M_{n-c}) because the elements f_j s_j map to zero in M_{n-c}, proving the Mittag-Leffler condition (proof lines 8983-8986).
proof_roadmap: Build the graded module of boundary images and check the grading.
Use finite generation to write every δ_n(s) over the finitely many generators.
Lift to M_{n+1} and read off the stable images.
difficulty_reason: The proof builds the graded module ⊕Im(δ_n) over the graded ring ⊕I^n/I^{n+1}, checks the grading via an explicit commutative diagram of short exact sequences, generates it by finitely many δ_{n_j}(s_j), and produces the stable-image constant c.
